newsitem.title: FRANCE: GAN says plans to cut 431 posts.
newsitem.headline: GAN says plans to cut 431 posts.

text.p: French state-owned insurer Groupe des Assurances Nationales (GAN) said on Wednesday that it planned to eliminate 431 posts over the next year as part a plan to cut operating costs and increase its competitiveness.
It said in a statement that it would eliminate 591 posts but create 160 new ones, resulting in a net reduction of 431 posts.
"A number of accompanying measures has been proposed with a view to limiting the number of layoffs," said GAN, which presented the plan on Wednesday to its staff works committee.
It said the plan, which would save 400 million francs over a full year, reflected a need for the group to become more competitive given the rapid consolidation of the French insurance industry.
Two of its rivals, Axa and UAP are merging to create the world's second-largest insurance group.
The French government recently suspended the privatisation of GAN's banking unit CIC, a sale that was supposed to raise funds to prepare GAN itself for privatisation.
European Commissioner Karel Van Miert said recently he expected the government to announce new state aid for GAN, which newspapers suggest could be in the region of 10 billion francs.

The company itself has declined to comment on possible further state aid, after an injection approved by Van Miert last year, and the finance ministry has yet to reveal its plans. (( -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452))
